terms.comment: Our working expression for source code: Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no term for it (Morgan–Owens has fōns for a source of information, s.v. source). Fontālis, of a source, is medieval Latin, the word from which English has “fontal” (New English Dictionary s.v. fontal: “med.L. fontālis”); it is not in Lewis & Short, whose adjectives are fontānus and fontāneus, of a spring. The noun is fōns, fontis m., a spring or source; the ō of the nominative is long before ns, and is not carried into fontis or fontālis.

sources: Lewis & Short: codex · Lewis & Short: fons · Morgan–Owens: Silva
James A. H. Murray (ed.), A New English Dictionary on Historical Principles (1901), s.v. fontal.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. source.
